title: Release Pathflow: Guided Branching for Incremental Model Variant Releases
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and prototype a guided "Release Pathflow" composer inside Redwood Console that helps engineers create branching release plans for model variants (canary -> staged A/B -> scale-up -> rollback). The focus is reducing operator error when creating complex multi-variant rollouts and making rollback paths discoverable and testable before traffic changes go live. This ticket covers UX flows, hi-fi prototypes, and a design review with Product and Eng to validate feasibility and SLO interactions.
goals: Provide a step-by-step guided composer for multi-variant releases that enforces safety gates
Make rollback paths explicit and previewable before applying changes
Surface truncated cost and latency impact for each branching step
Allow saving reusable release templates and exporting them as YAML for Dedicated/Private deployments
success_metrics: Reduce rollbacks caused by misconfigured traffic splits by 60% in pilot accounts
95% of release creators can complete a staged rollout flow in under 4 minutes in usability testing
Template reuse: 30% of teams reuse saved release templates within 6 weeks
assumptions: Backend will expose a policy API to validate safety gate conditions (error rate, latency thresholds)
Runtime can accept a declarative rollout plan with branching and revert actions
Console will be able to call a simulation endpoint to render expected metrics for a rollout step

decisions: MVP will support branching depth up to 3 and at most 4 concurrent variants per branch to limit complexity
Expose cost & latency delta as an optional expanded panel to avoid overwhelming users
Include an explicit 'rollback action' node that can be attached to any prior step and tested via dry-run
Save templates as named objects in Console so Platform teams can publish vetted rollout plans
tradeoffs: Limited branching depth reduces simulation accuracy for very complex release flows but keeps backend simulate costs bounded
Opting to hide cost details by default improves first-time user clarity but may frustrate power users — addressed by quick expand controls
Adding dry-run increases confidence but requires historical trace storage or sampled telemetry access which ups infra cost
accessibility_considerations: Keyboard-first navigation for composer canvas and step cards
ARIA labels for all step actions and safety-gate status
High-contrast badges and color-blind friendly palettes for variant indicators
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi prototype with flows for create/edit/preview/simulate/save-template (owner: Sophie)
